Tom —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a concise MAP and an evaluation plan summary; below is a distilled acceptance criteria and test plan so we can iterate quickly in thread. We'll own coordination and test execution.

High-level MAP milestones (owner):
- Pre-flight: ingest sample prompts and service account access (Velocity) — due Sep 8
- Pre-run smoke: Redwood runs baseline SFTL profile in a staging VPC with your sample prompts (Aditya) — Sep 9-10
- Formal acceptance tests: joint run (Redwood + Velocity + Latency Labs) — target Sep 16-17
- Results review & sign-off: Velocity Product + Procurement (Tom + Ops) — Sep 20
- Contract close / SOW signature: legal/procurement (Velocity) — Sep 24

Evaluation plan (overview):
- Workloads: 3 prompt buckets (short clinical triage, medium narrative summaries, long-context handovers) — provided in velocity_sample_prompts.jsonl
- Scenarios: (A) single-stream interactive chat (human-in-the-loop), (B) multi-turn scripted session, (C) burst concurrency spike (ramp to target)
- Measurement windows: 30-minute sustained window at target concurrency and a 10-minute spike window

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail rules):
- Time-to-first-token (SFTL / TTFT) measured end-to-end with streaming enabled on Redwood API:
  - p50 <= 200 ms
  - p95 <= 450 ms
  - p99 <= 900 ms
- Sustained throughput: 95th percentile token throughput >= 1,000 tokens/sec measured over 30 minutes
- Concurrency resilience: 150 concurrent streaming sessions (steady-state) with SFTL p95 not degrading > 20% from baseline
- Correctness: generated responses must pass a lightweight QA smoke-check defined in the prompt harness (>= 95% pass on intent match)

Pass rule: all SFTL targets and throughput must be met in the primary scenario (A) for the main prompt bucket. If any single metric misses by <= 10% we allow a single retest after a 24-hour remediation window. If misses > 10% or multiple metrics fail, we move to an engineering remediation plan and re-run within 72 hours.

Pre-flight requirements (Velocity):
- Provide service account + sample prompts (by Sep 8)
- Confirm IP allowlist for Redwood test harness
- Share representative session telemetry schema if available

Attachments included: sftl_test_harness.yaml (test runner config), velocity_sample_prompts.jsonl, load_profile_q3.csv, velocity_map_v1.pdf

If this looks good I'll coordinate a short 30-min tech run-through with Aditya to validate the harness and get the exact test windows locked.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick technical notes and a proposed measurement approach.

Measurement approach:
- Test harness: we will run the attached sftl_test_harness.yaml against a staging cluster that mirrors your dedicated profile (same model family + quantization). Tests will stream tokens to the client and timestamp at these points: request send, server first byte, client first token render.
- Clock sync: tests use NTP and server-side timestamps to avoid client clock drift (we'll collect both client and server timestamps).
- Sample sizes: each prompt bucket will run 500 sessions for p50/p95 stability; for p99 we'll aggregate 2,000 session samples across multiple runs.
- Warm-up: 10-minute warm-up at 20% target traffic to pre-populate KV caches and measure baseline.

Operational knobs we'll vary during tests (controlled variables):
- Batching profile (small/medium/large)
- KV cache hit-rate (simulate cold vs warm start)
- Sequence length (short/medium/long)

Pre-flight ask from Velocity:
- Provide 50 representative session recordings or example prompts (redact PHI) — we prefer JSONL format (velocity_sample_prompts.jsonl)
- Approve a test IP range and a short-lived API key for the staging run

I will own the staging run and produce a detailed CSV with per-request timestamps and summary percentiles, plus a side-by-side comparison to your on-prem baseline if you share telemetry.

On timing: Sep 9-10 for smoke is doable; formal run Sep 16-17 also looks good from our capacity perspective — I can lead the run on the 16th afternoon (PDT) if that aligns.
